issues.description: Return type mismatch for Farm.singFarmSong() and Farm.singFarmSongVerse(...): the UML/problem specification declares these methods as void (they should print the song), and the template also declares singFarmSong() as void and shows singFarmSongVerse as a void helper. The solution implementation, however, defines singFarmSong() to return String and singFarmSongVerse(Animal) to return String. This discrepancy can confuse students about whether the methods should print directly or return the song text, and may lead to inconsistent implementations or test mismatches.
issues.suggestedFix: Align the solution with the specification and template: change the solution methods to void and perform direct printing (i.e., singFarmSong(): void and singFarmSongVerse(Animal): void), or alternatively update the UML/problem statement and template to explicitly expect String return values. Preferably keep the methods void to match the pedagogical intent of printing the song.

issues.description: Parameter mismatch for Farm.singFarmSongVerse: the UML/problem statement specifies singFarmSongVerse(animal: Animal), and the solution implements singFarmSongVerse(Animal animal). In the template, however, the parameter is commented out and the method signature currently has no formal parameter (private void singFarmSongVerse(/*Animal animal*/)), which contradicts the UML and the solution. This commented-out parameter in the template can mislead students about the intended helper signature and hinder correct implementation.
issues.suggestedFix: Uncomment and restore the parameter in the template helper signature to match the UML and solution: change the template method declaration to private void singFarmSongVerse(Animal animal) (or private String singFarmSongVerse(Animal animal) if you decide to adopt the solution's return type), and update the method body accordingly. This makes the template consistent with the specification and intended design.
